item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows equilateral triangle $ABC$ with $AB=BC=CA$ and midpoint $D$ of side $BC$. Omar has already shown $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle ACD$.

Which claim correctly uses that congruence?

options.A: Corresponding parts are equal, so $\angle BAD=\angle CAD$, and each angle of equilateral $\triangle ABC$ measures $60^\circ$.
options.B: Equal angles at $A$ force the congruence of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACD$, so the congruence is not needed.
options.C: Congruence of the triangles is enough even if the vertex matching is ignored.
options.D: Only sides can be equal from congruence; the $60^\circ$ angle facts need a separate rule outside corresponding parts.
